title: Young life: Why I’m moving in with a married couple
gist: A 27-year-old London writer explains moving in with her boyfriend plus another married couple to cut costs in London's rental market while keeping separate bedrooms, framing it as gen Z inventing new living arrangements amid housing, cost-of-living and youth unemployment crises.

insights.claim: Facing the cost of living, unaffordable housing and youth unemployment, gen Z will have to find new ways of living rather than follow the traditional couple-household path.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Shared multi-couple renting points to demand for larger rental units and co-living formats.
insights.quote: Amid numerous crises (the cost of living, climate change, unaffordable housing, youth unemployment etc), I believe gen Z will have to find new ways of living.

insights.claim: Two couples pooling four incomes are searching for three-bedroom east London rentals at £3,000-£4,000 per month.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Signals high London rent levels pushing young professionals into group tenancies.

insights.claim: The author keeps a separate bedroom from her partner partly to avoid the financial precarity of a shared-room, lower-rent arrangement if the relationship ends.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Preference for private rooms sustains demand for more bedrooms per household.

insights.claim: Millennial couples who broke up but could not afford to move out were stuck either boomeranging to the family home or living with their ex.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Housing unaffordability creates relationship lock-in, a social cost of high rents.

insights.claim: Social-media algorithms present young adults with a set menu of lifestyle options (longevity optimisation, suburban domesticity, emigration) inherited from millennials, which the author rejects.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Wellness and lifestyle consumer trends may not transfer cleanly to gen Z.

insights.claim: The author prioritises friendships alongside romance and questions the primacy of the nuclear-household model of meet, date, cohabit, marry, have children.
insights.speaker: Alice Garnett
insights.so_what: Delayed family formation affects housing, fertility and consumption patterns.
